Abstract excerpt: Pedestrian simulators need a behaviour rule for every agent, but privacy usually limits the data for setting one to aggregate statistics, namely zone-level device counts and origin-to-destination (OD) flows, with no individual trajectories. Such aggregates under-determine individual behaviour, because many different sets of decisions reproduce the same counts. We fine-tune a language model crowd agent so that the simulated population matches the observed destination composition, the fraction of the departing crowd heading to each point of interest.
